info.title: GamePedia Cross-Platform Gate API
info.description: Machine-readable subset for the GamePedia 2.0 iOS/Android contract gate. This is not the complete backend API. Dates are RFC 3339 UTC date-time strings; image URLs are absolute HTTP(S) URLs or null.

get.description: Public endpoint (no authentication required; an Authorization header, valid or not, does not change behavior). Resolves the keyword through local alias/normalization rules, queries the IGDB provider, ranks the merged results, and returns at most `limit` games. Results may be served from a server-side cache (about 10 minutes TTL). `results` is an exact duplicate of `games` kept for released iOS 2.0 clients; new clients should read `games`.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search keyword. Trimmed server-side; 1-100 characters after trimming.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of games to return. Defaults to 20.

200.description: Search completed. An empty `games` array with `meta.resultCount` = 0 is a successful response, not an error.

400.description: Request validation failed. `error.code` is `INVALID_SEARCH_QUERY` when `q` is missing/empty/too long, `INVALID_GAMES_LIMIT` when `limit` is outside 1-30 or not an integer, otherwise `VALIDATION_ERROR`.

429.description: The IGDB provider is rate limited and no cached result could satisfy the request. `error.code` is `IGDB_RATE_LIMITED`. Clients should back off and retry later; cached searches may still succeed during the cooldown.

500.description: Server-side failure. `error.code` is `IGDB_NOT_CONFIGURED` when provider credentials are absent, otherwise `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`.

502.description: Provider failure. `error.code` is `IGDB_UPSTREAM_ERROR` (IGDB unreachable, non-OK, or invalid JSON) or `TWITCH_AUTH_UNAVAILABLE` (provider token endpoint failure). Messages never include provider payloads or credentials.

get.description: Public endpoint (no authentication required). Same keyword resolution pipeline as /games/search but returns a compact suggestion DTO capped at 8 items. Results may be served from a server-side cache (about 10 minutes TTL).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search keyword. Trimmed server-side; 1-100 characters after trimming.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of suggestions to return. Defaults to 6.

200.description: Suggestions computed. An empty `suggestions` array with `meta.resultCount` = 0 is a successful response.

400.description: Request validation failed. `error.code` is `INVALID_SEARCH_QUERY` when `q` is missing/empty/too long, `INVALID_GAMES_LIMIT` when `limit` is outside 1-8 or not an integer, otherwise `VALIDATION_ERROR`.

429.description: The IGDB provider is rate limited and no cached result could satisfy the request. `error.code` is `IGDB_RATE_LIMITED`.

500.description: Server-side failure. `error.code` is `IGDB_NOT_CONFIGURED` when provider credentials are absent, otherwise `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`.

post.summary: Create an account with email and password

deviceName.description: Optional human-readable device label stored with the refresh session (trimmed; 1-100 characters). Omitted or null keeps the session unlabeled; on refresh, omitting it preserves the rotated session’s previous label.

201.description: Account created; a session (user + token pair) is issued immediately.

400.description: Request validation failed (`VALIDATION_ERROR` with field details).

409.description: `EMAIL_ALREADY_IN_USE` or `NICKNAME_ALREADY_EXISTS`. Stable under concurrent duplicate signups.

post.summary: Log in with email and password

deviceName.description: Optional human-readable device label stored with the refresh session (trimmed; 1-100 characters). Omitted or null keeps the session unlabeled; on refresh, omitting it preserves the rotated session’s previous label.

200.description: New session issued. Existing sessions on other devices remain valid (multi-device policy).

401.description: `INVALID_CREDENTIALS`. The response does not reveal whether the email exists.

post.description: Verifies the Apple identity token (RS256, Apple JWKS, issuer and audience pinned). First login links or creates an account by verified email; subsequent logins resolve the stored (provider, subject) link. Concurrent first logins produce exactly one social link.

deviceName.description: Optional human-readable device label stored with the refresh session (trimmed; 1-100 characters). Omitted or null keeps the session unlabeled; on refresh, omitting it preserves the rotated session’s previous label.

200.description: Session issued for the linked account.

400.description: `APPLE_IDENTITY_TOKEN_REQUIRED` (missing token) or `APPLE_EMAIL_REQUIRED` (first login without an email claim).

409.description: `SOCIAL_ACCOUNT_CONFLICT`: the Apple subject is already linked to a different sign-in method.

503.description: `APPLE_AUTH_UNAVAILABLE`: Apple JWKS could not be fetched.

post.description: Verifies the Google ID token (RS256, Google JWKS, issuer and audience pinned). First login links to an existing account only when the Google email is authoritative (verified gmail.com or hosted-domain); otherwise a new account is created or `GOOGLE_ACCOUNT_LINK_CONFLICT` is returned. Concurrent first logins produce exactly one social link.

deviceName.description: Optional human-readable device label stored with the refresh session (trimmed; 1-100 characters). Omitted or null keeps the session unlabeled; on refresh, omitting it preserves the rotated session’s previous label.

200.description: Session issued for the linked account.

503.description: `GOOGLE_AUTH_UNAVAILABLE`: Google JWKS could not be fetched.

post.description: Atomically claims the presented refresh token (database compare-and-swap on `revokedAt IS NULL`) and issues a successor session in the same transaction. For any number of concurrent requests with the same token, exactly one succeeds; every loser and every later replay receives `401 TOKEN_REVOKED`. The success body contains BOTH the user and the rotated token pair.

deviceName.description: Optional human-readable device label stored with the refresh session (trimmed; 1-100 characters). Omitted or null keeps the session unlabeled; on refresh, omitting it preserves the rotated session’s previous label.

200.description: Rotation succeeded: the presented token is now revoked and `data.tokens` is its only successor.

401.description: `TOKEN_REVOKED` (already consumed, concurrent loser, or logged out), `TOKEN_EXPIRED`, or `UNAUTHORIZED` (bad signature, wrong token type, or subject mismatch).

404.description: `ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND`: the account no longer exists (for example after deletion).

post.description: Revokes only the presented refresh token (single-device logout); other sessions of the same user stay valid. Idempotent: repeating the call, or calling it with an unknown or already-revoked token, still returns 200. Possession of the token is the authorization; no access token is required.

200.description: The session is revoked (or was already invalid). A revoked token can never rotate again.
Always 200 with a fixed message; account existence is never revealed.

post.description: Claims the emailed reset token atomically (single use) and, in the same transaction, updates the password and deletes ALL refresh sessions of the user. Concurrent attempts with the same token allow exactly one success.

200.description: Password updated; every existing refresh session is invalidated.

404.description: `ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND`: the account behind the token no longer exists.

delete.description: Transactionally deletes the account and all of its refresh sessions (plus dependent rows via ON DELETE CASCADE). Afterwards no access or refresh token of the user can authenticate.

200.description: Account deleted; all sessions are invalid.

404.description: `ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND`: already deleted (repeat calls are rejected, not idempotent-success).

Recommend games using one accepted friend's visible signals

put.summary: Register or transfer a push token

delete.description: Accepts deviceId/token in query for deployed iOS compatibility or in a JSON body; conflicting duplicate inputs are rejected.

games.description: Ranked results, at most `limit` items. Canonical field for new clients.

results.description: Exact duplicate of `games`. iOS 2.0 compatibility alias; do not use in new clients.

suggestions.description: Compact companion suggestions derived from the same ranked result set.

coverUrl.description: Absolute https image URL (cover_big size) or null.

genres.description: Deduplicated genre names. Empty array when unknown.

platforms.description: Deduplicated platform names. Empty array when unknown.

rating.description: First available of totalRating, aggregatedRating, IGDB user rating.

releaseDate.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) of first release date, or null.

normalizedQuery.description: Lowercased/normalized form used for caching and ranking.

effectiveQuery.description: Query actually sent to the provider after alias resolution.

resultCount.description: Number of items in the returned list after applying `limit`.

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code. Search-related codes: INVALID_SEARCH_QUERY, INVALID_GAMES_LIMIT, VALIDATION_ERROR, IGDB_RATE_LIMITED, IGDB_UPSTREAM_ERROR, TWITCH_AUTH_UNAVAILABLE, IGDB_NOT_CONFIGURED, INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, NOT_FOUND. Auth-related codes: UNAUTHORIZED, TOKEN_EXPIRED, TOKEN_REVOKED, INVALID_CREDENTIALS, ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND, ACCOUNT_INACTIVE, ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED, EMAIL_ALREADY_IN_USE, NICKNAME_ALREADY_EXISTS, PASSWORD_RESET_TOKEN_INVALID, PASSWORD_RESET_TOKEN_USED, PASSWORD_RESET_TOKEN_EXPIRED, APPLE_IDENTITY_TOKEN_REQUIRED, APPLE_EMAIL_REQUIRED, APPLE_EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED, APPLE_AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN, APPLE_IDENTITY_TOKEN_EXPIRED, APPLE_AUTH_UNAVAILABLE, APPLE_AUTH_NOT_CONFIGURED, GOOGLE_ID_TOKEN_REQUIRED, GOOGLE_EMAIL_REQUIRED, GOOGLE_EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED, GOOGLE_AUTH_INVALID_TOKEN, GOOGLE_ID_TOKEN_EXPIRED, GOOGLE_AUTH_UNAVAILABLE, GOOGLE_AUTH_NOT_CONFIGURED, GOOGLE_ACCOUNT_LINK_CONFLICT, SOCIAL_ACCOUNT_CONFLICT, CONFLICT.

message.description: Human-readable message. Sanitized server-side; may be localized. Clients must branch on `code`, never on `message`.

details.description: Optional structured details. For validation failures this is an array of {field, message}.

field.description: Dot-joined path of the invalid input, e.g. "q" or "limit".

message.description: Sanitized validation message. Not stable; do not branch on it.

AuthUser.description: Public representation of the authenticated account. Never contains password hashes or token material.

profileImageUrl.description: Absolute URL when set; null when the account has no profile image.

AuthTokenPair.description: A freshly issued session. The refresh token is single-use: the first successful POST /auth/refresh with it revokes it and returns a successor.

accessToken.description: Short-lived JWT bearer token for Authorization headers.

refreshToken.description: Long-lived single-use JWT. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored server-side.

message.description: Fixed acknowledgement text. The response is identical whether or not the email exists; clients must not infer account existence.

bearerAuth.description: Short-lived JWT access token issued by the auth endpoints. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>`.
